2.2.3.2 Fauna
The southern bald eagle (Halieaetus leucocephalus leucocephalus), American peregrine falcon (Falco peregrinus anatum), and eastern cougar (Felis concolor cougar) are classed as endangered in the United States List of Endangered Fauna, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (1974). An identical classification has been assigned these species by North and South Carolina; North Carolina Department of Natural and Economic Resources (1973); Joyner, (1974). Sightings of these endangered species have not been confirmed within the proposed Bad Creek Project boundary, but these species may occur in the region based on past known nesting sites and range distributions. Only rarely would sightings be expected within the project area.
A bald eagle was reported at Lake Keowee by the Applicant's staff during the morning of August 18, 1974 (letter from the South Carolina Wildlife and Marine Resources Department, 1974). No peregrine falcon sightings have been reported; yet the area lies within the former range of the resident race of this species. A program to reestablish a self-sustaining breeding population of peregrine falcons to the 1940 level in areas of their former range in the eastern United States (east of the 100th meridian) is currently in the preliminary planning stage.
Review of the Preliminary List of Endangered Plant and Animal Species in North Carolina indicates the classification of a number of species in the undetermined category.
